checkResults.proofLimit: 15 field tests pass, of which 10 directly exercise the offline queue against an injected storage adapter, plus the DSH suite exits zero. This is real behavioural coverage of legacy recovery, terminal-failure evacuation and capacity exhaustion, executed in Node rather than on a device; it does not prove process death, encrypted-store behaviour or network toggling.

closureRule: Queued work must survive an authorized restart, never cross actor scope, reconcile safely, and surface terminal failure without false success.

defectsFoundAndFixed.summary: prepareFieldOfflineQueue deleted the v1 queue keys outright on every app start, destroying governed field work captured offline on an earlier build while the worker believed it was saved.
defectsFoundAndFixed.rootCause: A storage-generation bump shipped with no recovery path. v1 entries carry no actorId or installationId, so replaying them would cross actor scopes; deletion was the safe choice but doing it silently was the defect.
defectsFoundAndFixed.fix: v1 payloads are copied verbatim into a scoped recovery store before the legacy keys are released, and DshFieldSurface renders a warning so the worker knows to redo the affected work.
defectsFoundAndFixed.secondaryFinding: Legacy recovery previously ran through the injectable adapter, which is SecureStore in production, while v1 actually wrote to AsyncStorage. A dedicated legacy-storage seam now reads where v1 wrote; without it the recovery would have found nothing on a real device.
defectsFoundAndFixed.regressionTests: apps/app-field/runtime/tests/offline-queue-legacy-migration.test.mjs — 6 tests, all failing against the pre-fix source and passing after.

defectsFoundAndFixed.summary: Operations that reached failed_permanent were never removed from the live queue, so accumulated server refusals eventually exhausted queue capacity and every subsequent offline capture was rejected.
defectsFoundAndFixed.rootCause: purgeSyncedOperations removed only synced work and getDueOperations skipped terminal work, leaving terminal entries with no retention policy. Nothing in the codebase read failed_permanent, so the loss was also invisible to the worker.
defectsFoundAndFixed.fix: evacuateTerminalOperations moves terminal entries into the same scoped recovery store during each drain, freeing capacity and reporting the count through the existing surface notice.
defectsFoundAndFixed.regressionTests: apps/app-field/runtime/tests/offline-queue-terminal-capacity.test.mjs — 4 tests; the capacity test proves the brick by asserting that enqueue is rejected with `capacity exceeded` before evacuation and succeeds after.

cleanup: Removed getPendingCount, which had no consumer on any surface.

Removed a v2 migration branch written during this round after git history proved it unreachable: at the v2 commit no call site ever invoked configureFieldOfflineQueueScope, and requireScope() throws when unconfigured, so no device could persist v2 work.
